high.title: USD hits ceiling rate, free market exceeds 27,000 VND/USD
high.summary: The Vietnamese dong has weakened sharply against the USD as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East escalate. The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) quoted the USD/VND central rate at 25,059, up 2 dong. Commercial banks are now quoting USD at the ceiling rate of 26,311 VND/USD for selling, with buying rates rising dramatically - Vietcombank increased buying rates by 40 dong to 26,041 VND/USD, while VietinBank raised buying rates by 57 dong. The free market has pushed USD above 27,000 VND/USD for the first time, reflecting massive pressure on the dong. This represents the steepest VND depreciation in months, directly linked to global USD strength amid Middle East conflict fears. FX traders should expect continued pressure on VND as risk-off sentiment persists and oil prices remain elevated. The SBV may need to intervene more aggressively to prevent further devaluation if geopolitical tensions worsen.

high.title: Middle East tensions' impact on USD prices
high.summary: USD/VND exchange rate pressure has intensified due to Middle East conflicts. SBV's Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha noted that escalating tensions have driven global oil prices up 8-13% in days, creating additional inflationary pressure worldwide. This has made major central banks more cautious about rate cuts, with some even signaling potential rate hikes. At Vietnamese banks, USD is quoted around 26,029-26,309 VND (buy-sell), while free market rates reached 26,850-26,880 VND. The central rate has increased 13 dong over one week to 25,057 VND/USD. This reflects broader USD strength internationally amid heightened geopolitical risk. Bond investors should monitor whether continued USD strength and inflation fears delay expected Fed rate cuts, potentially keeping Vietnamese bond yields elevated and maintaining pressure on the dong.

high.title: USD and oil surge due to Middle East conflict: How will exchange rates and inflation in Vietnam be affected?
high.summary: The US-Israel strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, followed by Iranian retaliation, have created immediate global market impacts. Oil prices surged due to supply disruption fears, while logistics costs are rising dramatically. The USD Index (DXY) jumped 0.8% to 98.42 points, with gold also rising as "risk-off" sentiment dominates. VCBS analysis indicates that in this uncertain geopolitical environment, global capital flows are reallocating toward safe-haven assets like USD and gold. For Vietnam, this creates dual pressure: import inflation from higher oil prices and currency depreciation pressure as USD strengthens. Vietnamese government bond yields may face upward pressure if the SBV needs to raise rates to defend the dong or if inflation expectations rise significantly. FX traders should prepare for continued volatility until geopolitical tensions ease.

medium.title: VN-Index lost more than 113 points in 1 week, experts name stock groups in "oversold zone"
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market ended the first week of March negatively with VN-Index dropping to 1,767 points, losing over 113 points compared to the previous week. The decline was triggered by escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions, similar to the "tariff shock" in April 2025. Foreign investors continued strong net selling despite Vietnam's potential FTSE Russell upgrade consideration in about one month.

medium.title: BIDV interest rates March 2025: Which term has the highest interest rate?
medium.summary: BIDV maintains stable deposit rates in March 2026. Counter deposit rates range from 0.1% for non-term deposits to 5.3% for 24-36 month terms. Short-term rates (1-2 months) are at 2.1%, while 12-month terms offer 5.2%. The highest rates of 5.3% apply to long-term deposits of 24 months and above.

medium.title: Military Bank just increased savings interest rates sharply
medium.summary: MB Bank has increased deposit rates significantly for terms 12 months and above. Rates for 12-18 month terms rose from 5.5% to 6.1% (up 0.6 percentage points), while 24-60 month terms increased from 6.3% to 6.6%. Short-term rates under 12 months remained unchanged, indicating banks are competing for longer-term funding sources.

medium.title: Vietcombank latest interest rates March 2026
medium.summary: Vietcombank maintains stable deposit rate structure in early March 2026. The highest rates remain at 5.3% for terms 24 months and above, applied to both counter and online deposits. Counter deposit rates range from 0.10% for non-term to 5.20% for 12-month terms, showing continued stability in funding costs for the largest bank.

medium.title: Experts: Securities market next week may fall to 1,700 points
medium.summary: Vietnam stock market experienced a turbulent first week of March amid global financial market volatility due to escalating Middle East tensions. VN-Index lost 112.49 points (-5.98%) to 1,767.84 points with liquidity 50% higher than 20-week average. Foreign investors continued heavy net selling worth over 6,000 billion VND despite approaching FTSE Russell upgrade review.
